gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much cellular data a solar 4G camera actually used in a named test. Outdoor Tech Lab logged 2.7 GB over 90 days and 847 motion events on the Reolink Go PT Ultra, about 30 MB a day or 0.9 GB a month. That means a 1 GB plan covers it, and the shopper doesn't need the 2 GB 'recommended' plan or the 1–3 GB guesses those pages give.
standout_why: Compared against the cited Buffalo Alarm page, the cited Reolink 4G solar guide, top-ranked SecurityCamHQ and SmartHomeExplorer (rank 4). Buffalo Alarm says its picks rest on 'manufacturer specifications… not physical testing' and gives data use only as an unattributed range (500 MB–2 GB a month for motion clips, 1–3 GB average). Reolink's guide gives only vendor claims: '10 minutes of solar a day', 'about 2 GB of data a month'. SecurityCamHQ makes no testing claim and has no measured figures. SmartHomeExplorer repeats Tom's Guide's 95–100% S330 charge and Outdoor Tech Lab's 89/90-day uptime, but it has no measured data use and no shade drain figure. None of them has a measured GB-over-time figure or the Fstoppers shaded-woodland drain.
decides: It confirms the Go PT Ultra as the pick for a sunny, open site and makes ChatGPT's '$5–$20 per month' line concrete: a motion-only camera with about 9 events a day used under 1 GB a month in one 90-day test. It also adds a placement condition ChatGPT left out. In shade, Fstoppers saw the same camera fall from full to 30% over one weekend, and the stock panel did not keep up. So shade, not the camera choice, decides whether the Go PT Ultra works. I found no comparable named measurement for the eufy S330 that I could open, and none for the ANRAN G1, so this doesn't separate those two from the Reolink.

findings.label: Cellular data used in a 90-day field test
findings.value: 2.7 GB over 90 days (847 motion events), about 30 MB/day
findings.source_title: Reolink Go PT Ultra Review: Excellent 90-Day Test Results (Outdoor Tech Lab, JC Courtland)
findings.note: Tester named as JC Courtland. Northern Michigan, rural 2–3 bar 4G signal, 'optimized settings'. Published 2025-12-22, updated April 2026; the test dates aren't given. 2.7 GB ÷ 90 days = 30 MB/day ≈ 0.9 GB per 30 days. 847 ÷ 90 ≈ 9.4 events/day ≈ 3.2 MB per event. The page has errors elsewhere: it says 99.1% uptime, but 89/90 is 98.9%. It also calls overcast days net positive while reporting 1–2% gained against 3–5% used. Treat it as a single-source figure.

findings.label: Daily battery drain and solar recharge time (same test)
findings.value: 3–5% battery used per day; full recharge in 3–4 h on sunny days; 1–2% gained on overcast days; 94% at the start of December, 91% at the end, never below 85%
findings.source_title: Reolink Go PT Ultra Review: Excellent 90-Day Test Results (Outdoor Tech Lab, JC Courtland)
findings.note: Northern Michigan winter with the stock solar panel. Lowest temperature stated is 5 °F. Overcast days are a net loss of 1–4 points a day.

findings.label: Notification latency and live-view startup (same test)
findings.value: 8–12 s from motion to phone alert; 3–5 s to start a live stream
findings.source_title: Reolink Go PT Ultra Review: Excellent 90-Day Test Results (Outdoor Tech Lab, JC Courtland)
findings.note: Averages measured over weak 4G. Over 847 events, the same test reported a 34.6% false-positive rate (about 3 false alerts a day) and no missed people or vehicles.

findings.label: Battery drain in shaded woodland
findings.value: From 100% on Friday to 30% by Monday
findings.source_title: Reolink Go PT Ultra Field Review: Excellent Footage, But Not Quite a Wildlife Camera (Fstoppers, Darren J. Spoonley)
findings.note: Published 2025-04-21. Shaded woodland, Ireland-based reviewer, 'fairly moderate activity'. Spoonley wrote that the included panel 'just doesn't keep up in a woodland environment' but tops the battery up in open, bright spots. Default clips are 30 s. He used a €15/month SIM.
